question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

The nation pursued a policy of autorky, producing everything it needed within its own borders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Autarky.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "autorky", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Autarky". (आत्मनिर्भरता अथवा स्वावलंबन)

 

• Autarky means a state of self-sufficiency, especially economic independence achieved by a nation without relying on external trade or aid.
◦ Example: North Korea has often been cited as a modern example of a country striving for economic autarky.

 

• Spelling key: AUT + ARK + Y — remember it as "AUTo-ARK" (self-contained, like an ark carrying everything it needs). Note the single "r" and the ending "-arky", not "-arkey" or "-orky".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Autarcky" — incorrect; adds a superfluous "c" that does not belong in the word.

 

• Option 3: "Autorky" — incorrect; wrongly changes the second vowel to "o" instead of "a".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence does contain a genuine misspelling ("autorky"), so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related root words include autarch, autarchic, and the political term autarchy (absolute sovereignty) — a different but easily confused word from autarky (self-sufficiency).

 

• Other commonly misspelled Greek-rooted political/economic terms: *autonomy, autocracy, oligarchy* — watch the vowel placement carefully in each.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Schizotipal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Schizotipal". The correct spelling is "Schizotypal", retaining the "y" from its Greek root *schizein* (to split). (सिज़ोटाइपल - व्यक्तित्व की एक विशेष शैली जिसमें असामान्य विचार व सामाजिक असहजता होती है)
◦ Example: People with schizotypal personality traits often have eccentric beliefs and discomfort in close relationships.

 

• Spelling rule: Schizotypal is built from schizo- (Greek *schizein*, "to split") plus -typal (Greek *typos*, "type/pattern") — it is this second part that keeps the "y", just as in type, typical, and prototype. Replacing the "y" with an "i" (as in "Schizotipal") is a very common error because the resulting sound is nearly identical.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Camouflage" — correctly spelt; from French, meaning to disguise or conceal.

 

• Option 3: "Melancholic" — correctly spelt; relating to melancholy or deep sadness.

 

• Option 4: "Idiosyncrasy" — correctly spelt; a distinctive individual characteristic or habit.

 

NOTE

 

• Words sharing the typ- root (Greek *typos*, "type") that keep the "y": *type, typical, prototype, stereotype* — the same "y" that schizotypal keeps in its "-typal" ending.

 

• Other "-al" adjectives commonly misspelled by vowel confusion: *hypothetical, theoretical, categorical, atypical*.

 

• Exam strategy: read unfamiliar technical/medical words syllable-by-syllable; the misspelling in such long words is usually a single swapped vowel in the middle, not the ending.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The professor explained that the laws of thermodinamics govern how energy is transferred within a system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thermodinamics.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "thermodinamics". The correct spelling is "thermodynamics", combining thermo- (heat) and dynamics (force/power). (ऊष्मागतिकी - भौतिकी की वह शाखा जो ऊष्मा और ऊर्जा के परिवर्तन का अध्ययन करती है)

 

• Thermodynamics is the branch of physics concerned with heat, energy, and the conversion of one into the other, and with how these affect matter.
◦ Example: The first law of thermodynamics states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The professor explained that the laws of thermodynamics govern how energy is transferred within a system.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "professor" — correctly spelt; a senior academic teacher.

 

• Option 2: "laws" — correctly spelt; plural of "law", a scientific principle.

 

• Option 4: "energy" — correctly spelt; the capacity to do work.

 

NOTE

 

• Words built on the Greek root dyna- (power/force) follow the same pattern.
◦ *dynamics -> dynamic -> dynamo -> dynamite*

 

• Compound scientific terms formed with thermo- (heat) keep the connecting vowel "o": *thermometer, thermostat, thermocouple* — never drop or replace it with "i" or "a".

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

As a passionate numesmatist, he spent years collecting rare ancient coins from around the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Numismatist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "numesmatist", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Numismatist". (मुद्राशास्त्री अर्थात सिक्कों का संग्रहकर्ता)

 

• A numismatist is a person who studies or collects coins, banknotes, and medals.
◦ Example: The numismatist proudly displayed a rare gold coin from the Gupta era at the exhibition.

 

• Spelling key: NUM + ISMA + TIST — remember the "i" after "num" (not "e"), as in numismatics, the study of currency. The word derives from Latin *numisma*, meaning "coin".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Numismattist" — incorrect; wrongly doubles the "t" before the suffix.

 

• Option 3: "Numesmatist" — incorrect; replaces the correct "i" after "num" with an "e".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence does contain a genuine misspelling ("numesmatist"), so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related word family: numismatics (the study of coins), numismatic (adjective), from Latin *numisma* / Greek *nomisma*, meaning "coin" or "currency".

 

• Other collector/specialist nouns ending in -ist with tricky internal vowels: *philatelist, archivist, linguist* — check each syllable carefully.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mitagate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Mitagate". The correct spelling is "Mitigate", from Latin *mitigare* ("to soften"). (कम करना अथवा शमन करना)
◦ Example: The government introduced new policies to mitigate the effects of the drought on farmers.

 

• Spelling rule: the second syllable of mitigate uses "i", not "a" — compare related words mitigation and mitigating, which keep the same "i". A useful memory trick: "mit-I-gate" has an "I" right in the middle, just like the idea of reducing or lightening a problem.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Reconcile" — correctly spelt; to restore friendly relations or make consistent.

 

• Option 3: "Perseverance" — correctly spelt; continued effort despite difficulty.

 

• Option 4: "Legitimate" — correctly spelt; conforming to the law or accepted standards.

 

NOTE

 

• Words sharing the -igate pattern: *litigate, instigate, navigate, investigate* — all keep the "i" before "gate", never "a".

 

• Other Latin-derived verbs often misspelled by vowel-swapping in the middle syllable: *deteriorate, calibrate, deliberate*.

 

• Exam strategy: when a word has a repeated vowel sound in different syllables (like the "a" sounds in mitigate), examiners often test whether you know which syllable actually uses which vowel letter.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The researchers measured the cytotoxisity of the new compound on cancer cells in the laboratory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cytotoxisity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "cytotoxisity". The correct spelling is "cytotoxicity", formed from cyto- (cell) + toxic + -ity. (कोशिका-विषाक्तता - किसी पदार्थ की कोशिकाओं को क्षति पहुँचाने की क्षमता)

 

• Cytotoxicity refers to the quality of being toxic to living cells, often measured to test the safety of drugs or chemicals.
◦ Example: High cytotoxicity in the tested compound suggested it was unsuitable for use in humans.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The researchers measured the cytotoxicity of the new compound on cancer cells in the laboratory.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "researchers" — correctly spelt; people who conduct scientific research.

 

• Option 3: "compound" — correctly spelt; a substance formed from two or more elements.

 

• Option 4: "cells" — correctly spelt; plural of "cell", the basic unit of life.

 

NOTE

 

• Words retaining the "-icity" suffix formed from "-ic" adjectives.
◦ *toxic -> toxicity, elastic -> elasticity, authentic -> authenticity*

 

• Compound biological terms beginning with cyto- (Greek for "cell") always keep the "y": *cytoplasm, cytology, cytoskeleton* — never replace it with "i".

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

After years of study, she specialized in otorinolaryngology, the branch of medicine dealing with ear, nose, and throat disorders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Otorhinolaryngology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "otorinolaryngology", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Otorhinolaryngology". (कर्ण-नासा-कंठ विज्ञान अर्थात कान, नाक और गले से संबंधित चिकित्सा शाखा)

 

• Otorhinolaryngology is the medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the ear, nose, and throat (also called ENT).
◦ Example: He visited a specialist in otorhinolaryngology after experiencing persistent ear infections.

 

• Spelling key: break it into its Greek roots — OTO (ear) + RHINO (nose) + LARYNGO (throat/larynx) + LOGY (study of). The commonly dropped letter is the silent "h" after "ot", as in rhino- (compare rhinoceros, rhinitis).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Otorinolaryngology" — incorrect; drops the essential "h" from the "rhino-" root.

 

• Option 3: "Otorhinolarynggology" — incorrect; wrongly doubles the "g" before "-ology".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence does contain a genuine misspelling ("otorinolaryngology"), so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related root words: rhinitis, rhinoplasty, rhinoceros (all keep "rh-" from Greek *rhis*, "nose"); laryngitis, laryngoscope (from *larynx*).

 

• Other long medical "-ology" compound terms often misspelled at their root joins: *gastroenterology, ophthalmology, otolaryngology* (a shorter synonym of this same word).

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Luxurient.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Luxurient". The correct spelling is "Luxuriant", ending in "-ant", not "-ent". (हराभरा अथवा प्रचुर - अत्यधिक वृद्धि या उगने वाला)
◦ Example: The garden was famous for its luxuriant growth of ferns and tropical flowers.

 

• Spelling rule: luxuriant comes from the verb luxuriate (to grow profusely) and keeps the -ant ending like other adjectives derived from Latin present-participle stems in -ans. Do not confuse it with words like reminiscent, fluorescent, or belligerent, which genuinely end in -ent because they derive from Latin -ens stems — the two groups must simply be memorised word by word.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Reminiscent" — correctly spelt; evoking memory of something.

 

• Option 3: "Fluorescent" — correctly spelt; emitting light through fluorescence.

 

• Option 4: "Belligerent" — correctly spelt; hostile and aggressive.

 

NOTE

 

• Words correctly ending in -ant like luxuriant: *exuberant, flamboyant, extravagant*.

 

• Words correctly ending in -ent that are often confused with the "-ant" group: *reminiscent, fluorescent, belligerent, benevolent*.

 

• Exam strategy: since "-ant" and "-ent" sound nearly identical when spoken, there is no shortcut rule that covers all cases — keep a personal revision list of high-frequency SSC words in each group.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

She sat by the window, wearing a pensitive expression as she watched the rain fall on the quiet street.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pensitive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "pensitive". The correct spelling is "pensive", meaning deeply or dreamily thoughtful. (चिंतनशील अथवा उदास भाव से सोच में डूबा हुआ)

 

• Pensive describes a state of being engaged in serious or wistful thought, often tinged with sadness.
◦ Example: He gazed out of the train window with a pensive look, lost in memories of home.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *She sat by the window, wearing a pensive expression as she watched the rain fall on the quiet street.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "window" — correctly spelt; an opening in a wall fitted with glass.

 

• Option 3: "rain" — correctly spelt; water falling in drops from clouds.

 

• Option 4: "street" — correctly spelt; a public road in a city or town.

 

NOTE

 

• Words ending in the simple -ive suffix (from Latin *-ivus*) without an inserted "t".
◦ pensive (from Latin *pensare*, "to weigh, ponder") follows the same "-ive" pattern as massive and passive — none of them insert a "t" before "-ive".

 

• Do not confuse the ending "-sive" pattern by inserting extra consonants; when in doubt, recall the base idea (pensive relates to pondering, not to "sensitive").

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

The committee voted to sensure the minister for his conduct during the negotiations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Censure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "sensure", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Censure". (निंदा करना अथवा औपचारिक रूप से कड़ी आलोचना करना)

 

• Censure means to formally express severe disapproval or criticism of someone, especially in an official capacity.
◦ Example: Parliament passed a motion to censure the official for misusing public funds.

 

• Spelling key: CEN + SURE — begins with "C", not "S", and is easily confused with the unrelated word censer (a container for burning incense) and the verb censor (to suppress content). Remember: cenSURe relates to formal disapproval.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Censer" — incorrect; this is a real but different word meaning a vessel for burning incense, not the target word.

 

• Option 3: "Sensure" — incorrect; wrongly begins with "S" instead of "C", matching the error in the sentence.

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence does contain a genuine misspelling ("sensure"), so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related but distinct words often confused with censure: censor (to suppress/ban content), censer (incense burner), census (official population count) — all share the "cens-" root but differ in meaning.

 

• Other formal-criticism vocabulary worth revising alongside censure: *reprimand, admonish, rebuke, denounce*.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Vibrent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Vibrent". The correct spelling is "Vibrant", ending in "-ant". (जीवंत अथवा स्पंदनशील - ऊर्जा और रंगों से भरपूर)
◦ Example: The market was full of vibrant colours, sounds, and the aroma of fresh spices.

 

• Spelling rule: vibrant derives from the Latin verb vibrare (to vibrate/shake) and follows the -ant pattern of adjectives formed from -are verbs (compare tolerant from *tolerare*, dominant from *dominari*). Words derived from Latin -ere/-ire verb stems more often take -ent (compare persistent from *persistere*).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Persistent" — correctly spelt; continuing firmly despite difficulty.

 

• Option 3: "Coherent" — correctly spelt; logical and consistent.

 

• Option 4: "Vigilant" — correctly spelt; watchful and alert.

 

NOTE

 

• Other -ant adjectives from Latin -are verbs: *tolerant, dominant, hesitant, vibrant*.

 

• Other -ent adjectives from Latin -ere/-ire verbs: *persistent, coherent, consistent, insistent*.

 

• Exam strategy: when unsure between "-ant" and "-ent", think of a related noun form — nouns ending in -ance usually pair with -ant adjectives (vibrance -> vibrant), while nouns ending in -ence usually pair with -ent adjectives (coherence -> coherent).

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The philosopher argued that true eudiamonia depends not on pleasure alone but on a life of virtuous activity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. eudiamonia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "eudiamonia". The correct spelling is "eudaimonia", with "ai" before "mon", not "ia". (सुख अथवा मानव उत्कर्ष - अरस्तू के दर्शन में जीवन की सर्वोच्च भलाई या फलना-फूलना)

 

• Eudaimonia is an ancient Greek term, central to Aristotle's ethics, referring to human flourishing or the highest good achieved through virtuous living, rather than mere pleasure.
◦ Example: Aristotle believed eudaimonia was achieved through a lifetime of rational and virtuous activity, not fleeting happiness.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The philosopher argued that true eudaimonia depends not on pleasure alone but on a life of virtuous activity.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "philosopher" — correctly spelt; a person who studies fundamental questions of existence and knowledge.

 

• Option 3: "pleasure" — correctly spelt; a feeling of happiness or enjoyment.

 

• Option 4: "activity" — correctly spelt; the state of being active or engaged in action.

 

NOTE

 

• Greek-derived philosophical terms keeping the diphthong "ai".
◦ eudaimonia -> *daimon* (Greek for "spirit"); aesthetic -> *aisthesis* (Greek for "perception") — both retain the "ai" from their Greek roots.

 

• A commonly accepted variant spelling, eudaemonia (with "ae" instead of "ai"), is also considered correct in many dictionaries — but transposing the letters to "ia" as in "eudiamonia" is a genuine error, not a recognised variant.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

Contrery to what many people believe, spicy food does not cause ulcers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Contrary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "Contrery", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Contrary". (विपरीत अथवा इसके विपरीत)

 

• Contrary means opposite in nature, direction, or meaning; it is often used in the phrase "contrary to" to introduce a statement that opposes a common belief.
◦ Example: Contrary to expectations, the small team won the championship against much stronger rivals.

 

• Spelling key: CONTR + ARY — note the "a" before "ry" (not "e"), matching the pattern of contra- (against), as in contradict and contravene.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Contrery" — incorrect; wrongly uses "e" instead of "a" before the final syllable, matching the error in the sentence.

 

• Option 3: "Contrarry" — incorrect; wrongly doubles the "r" before "y".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence does contain a genuine misspelling ("Contrery"), so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words sharing the contra- root (against/opposite): contradict, contravene, contrast, controversy.

 

• Other common "-ary" adjectives/nouns often misspelled with "e": *necessary, secretary, ordinary, temporary* — the ending is always "-ary", never "-ery".

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Palimsest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Palimsest". The correct spelling is "Palimpsest", keeping the "p" before "sest". (पुनर्लिखित पांडुलिपि - एक ऐसी पांडुलिपि जिस पर पुराना लेख मिटाकर नया लेख लिखा गया हो, परंतु पुराने लेख के चिह्न शेष रह जाएं)
◦ Example: Historians studied the ancient palimpsest to uncover the faint traces of an even older text beneath the visible one.

 

• Spelling rule: palimpsest comes from the Greek *palimpsestos* ("scraped again") — palin (again) + psen (to scrape). The middle "mp" cluster is often dropped in error; remembering the Greek root *palin* + *psestos* helps retain both consonants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Reconnaissance" — correctly spelt; military observation to gather information.

 

• Option 3: "Idiosyncratic" — correctly spelt; peculiar or individual in nature.

 

• Option 4: "Bureaucracy" — correctly spelt; a system of government administered by officials.

 

NOTE

 

• Words retaining tricky consonant clusters from Greek/Latin roots: *palimpsest (mp), diaphragm (gm/ph), phlegm (gm)*.

 

• Other words frequently misspelled by silently dropping a middle consonant: *government (n), foreign (g), Wednesday (d)*.

 

• Exam strategy: for long, low-frequency words like palimpsest, pronounce each syllable deliberately (pa-LIMP-sest) to "hear" the consonants that are easy to drop when reading quickly.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

Despite the chaos around her, she maintained her equanimaty while her colleagues grew increasingly anxious and irritable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. equanimaty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "equanimaty". The correct spelling is "equanimity", ending in "-imity", not "-imaty". (मानसिक शांति/धैर्य)

 

• It means the quality of being calm and composed, especially under pressure or in a difficult situation; from Latin *aequus* (equal) + *animus* (mind).
◦ Example: She accepted the unexpected news with remarkable equanimity.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *Despite the chaos around her, she maintained her equanimity while her colleagues grew increasingly anxious and irritable.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "colleagues" — correctly spelt; from French *collègue*, note the "-eagues" ending.

 

• Option 3: "anxious" — correctly spelt; ends in "-xious", not "-xous".

 

• Option 4: "irritable" — correctly spelt; double "r", single "t" — not the reverse.

 

NOTE

 

• Words formed with the Latin prefix *aequ-/equi-* (meaning "equal") often relate to balance and fairness.
◦ *equal -> equality*, *equidistant -> equidistance*, *equinox -> equinoctial*

 

• The abstract-noun suffix "-ity" (as in equanimity, serenity, sanity) is frequently misspelled with "-ety" or "-aty" — always check it against the base adjective form.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

After years of exposure to the sun, the old rubber seal had become brittel and cracked at the slightest touch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Brittle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "brittel", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "brittle". (भंगुर/आसानी से टूटने वाला)

 

• It means hard but easily broken or snapped; fragile.
◦ Example: Dry autumn leaves become brittle and crumble underfoot.

 

• Spelling key: BRIT + TLE — a double "t" followed by "-le", not "-el"; do not swap the last two letters as in the common error "brittel".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Brittel" — incorrect; wrongly swaps the last two letters ("-el" instead of "-le").

 

• Option 3: "Brittal" — incorrect; wrongly ends in "-al" instead of "-le".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the given sentence does contain a misspelling ("brittel"), so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related word family: brittleness (noun) — the double "t" is retained in all forms.

 

• Other commonly misspelled "-le" ending words: *little*, *subtle*, *supple*, *feeble* — remember "-le", not "-el", at the end.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Caustisity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Caustisity". The correct spelling is "Causticity", retaining the "-tic" of "caustic" before adding "-ity". (कटुता/तीखापन)
◦ Example: The causticity of his remarks left the audience stunned.

 

• When the suffix "-ity" is added to adjectives ending in "-tic" (e.g. *caustic*, *elastic*, *authentic*), the "-tic" is normally kept intact and only "-ity" is appended — caustic + ity = causticity, not "caustisity". Contrast this with adjectives ending in "-ant"/"-ent", which instead change to "-ance"/"-ence" (e.g. *elegant -> elegance*).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Bureaucracy" — correctly spelt; from French *bureau* + Greek *-kratia* (rule).

 

• Option 3: "Reminiscent" — correctly spelt; ends in "-scent", not "-scant".

 

• Option 4: "Consensus" — correctly spelt; note the middle "s" — "con-sen-sus", not "concensus" (a common error swaps this "s" for a "c").

 

NOTE

 

• Words retaining "-tic" before "-ity": *elastic -> elasticity*, *authentic -> authenticity*, *domestic -> domesticity*.

 

• Words often confused by a "c/s" swap: *concensus/consensus*, *decendant/descendant* — always check whether the sound is "s" or "sh" before deciding on "c" or "s".

 

• Exam strategy: when a word ends in "-city" or "-sity", say it slowly syllable by syllable to catch an extra or missing consonant.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The diplomat's witty persiflege concealed a shrewd understanding of the negotiations, and his colleagues found his nonchalant manner reassuring.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. persiflege.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "persiflege". The correct spelling is "persiflage", ending in "-flage", not "-flege". (हल्की-फुल्की छेड़छाड़/परिहास)

 

• It means light, teasing banter, or a frivolous, mocking way of treating a serious subject; borrowed directly from French.
◦ Example: Beneath the persiflage of the after-dinner speech lay a serious warning.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The diplomat's witty persiflage concealed a shrewd understanding of the negotiations, and his colleagues found his nonchalant manner reassuring.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "shrewd" — correctly spelt; note "-ew-", not "-ue-".

 

• Option 3: "negotiations" — correctly spelt; from "negotiate", single "t" before "-ions".

 

• Option 4: "nonchalant" — correctly spelt; French borrowing, ends in "-ant", not "-ent".

 

NOTE

 

• Many English words borrowed directly from French retain their original spelling and endings.
◦ *persiflage -> persiflage*, *camouflage -> camouflage*, *sabotage -> sabotage*

 

• General rule: French loanwords ending in the "-age" sound (pronounced "-ahzh") are spelt "-age", never "-edge" or "-ege" — a frequent source of spelling errors.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

Honesty and hard work form the very creed by which she lives her life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No replacement required.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The underlined word, "creed", is already spelt correctly in the sentence and needs no replacement. (धर्म/सिद्धांत या मूल विश्वास)

 

• It means a system of religious or other beliefs; a guiding set of principles.
◦ Example: Respect for all faiths is central to his personal creed.

 

• Spelling key: CREED — one syllable, double "e" in the middle; do not add a silent "e" at the end ("creede") or triple the "e" ("creeed").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Creede" — incorrect; wrongly adds a silent "e" at the end.

 

• Option 2: "Creed" — this is actually the correct spelling, exactly matching the word as used in the sentence; since "creed" is already spelt correctly, no replacement is required.

 

• Option 3: "Creeed" — incorrect; wrongly triples the "e".

 

NOTE

 

• Related word family: credo (Latin root, "I believe"), credence, credible — all trace back to Latin *credere*, to believe.

 

• Other short double-vowel words often misspelled: *deed*, *feed*, *greed*, *need* — the double letter stays in the middle, not at the end.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Deleterius.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Deleterius". The correct spelling is "Deleterious", ending in "-erious", not "-erius". (हानिकारक)
◦ Example: Smoking has a deleterious effect on health.

 

• Many Latin-derived adjectives end in "-ious" (meaning "full of" or "characterized by"), e.g. deleterious, *serious*, *mysterious* — the "-i-" before "-ous" is easy to drop by mistake, so always check for it; contrast this with adjectives that end in plain "-ous" with no "-i-", such as *dangerous* or *hazardous*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Reconnaissance" — correctly spelt; from French, double "n" and double "s".

 

• Option 3: "Camaraderie" — correctly spelt; note the single "m" and the "-derie" ending.

 

• Option 4: "Idiosyncrasy" — correctly spelt; ends in "-crasy", not "-cracy" (which relates to "rule", not "temperament").

 

NOTE

 

• Adjectives ending in "-ious" derived from Latin: *deleterious*, *mysterious*, *laborious*, *notorious* — always retain the "-i-" before "-ous".

 

• Contrast with plain "-ous" adjectives with no "-i-": *dangerous*, *hazardous*, *nervous* — these attach directly to a noun root.

 

• Exam strategy: when unsure whether a word ends in "-ous" or "-ious", think of its noun/verb root — a root ending in a vowel sound needing a linking "i" usually takes "-ious".

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

Despite the setbacks, the young entrepreneur remained sanguin about the company's prospects and refused to abandon her ambitious plans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sanguin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "sanguin". The correct spelling is "sanguine", retaining the final "-e". (आशावादी/प्रफुल्लित)

 

• It means optimistic or cheerful about the future, especially in a difficult situation; from Latin *sanguis* (blood), reflecting the old belief that a ruddy, blood-flushed complexion showed a cheerful temperament.
◦ Example: He remained sanguine even after losing his job.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *Despite the setbacks, the young entrepreneur remained sanguine about the company's prospects and refused to abandon her ambitious plans.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "entrepreneur" — correctly spelt; French borrowing, note the "-eur" ending.

 

• Option 3: "prospects" — correctly spelt; from Latin *prospectus*, "-ects" not "-ekts".

 

• Option 4: "ambitious" — correctly spelt; ends in "-itious", not "-itous".

 

NOTE

 

• Several English adjectives ending in a silent final "-e" are easy to misspell by dropping it:
◦ *sanguine -> sanguin*, *routine -> routin*, *genuine -> genuin* (all incorrect without the final "e")

 

• General rule: several French/Latin-derived adjectives conventionally retain a final silent "e" as part of their borrowed spelling — *sanguine*, *routine*, *genuine* — dropping it is a common but incorrect simplification, so always check the word against its full dictionary form.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

Everyone admired the Nobel gesture of the young boy who returned the lost wallet to its owner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Noble.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "Nobel", is misspelt in this context. The correct spelling is "Noble"; "Nobel" (as in the Nobel Prize) is a different word entirely and a classic SSC trap. (उदार/उच्च नैतिक गुणों वाला)

 

• It means having fine personal qualities or high moral principles; of impressive appearance or dignity.
◦ Example: He made a noble sacrifice for his family.

 

• Spelling key: NOBLE — ends in "-ble", not "-bel"; do not confuse it with the surname "Nobel" (as in Alfred Nobel / the Nobel Prize), which ends in "-bel".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Nobel" — incorrect here; this is a different real word (the surname in "Nobel Prize"), not a spelling variant of "noble".

 

• Option 3: "Nobol" — incorrect; wrongly uses "o" instead of "e" before the ending.

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence uses "Nobel", the wrong word here, so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related word family: nobility (noun), nobly (adverb) — all retain the "-bl-" root, unlike "Nobel".

 

• Commonly confused word pairs in SSC exams: *noble/Nobel*, *desert/dessert*, *stationary/stationery* — always check meaning, not just sound.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Expostalation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Expostalation". The correct spelling is "Expostulation", with "-stu-", not "-sta-". (कड़ी आपत्ति/उलाहना)
◦ Example: His expostulation against the unfair decision fell on deaf ears.

 

• The word comes from the verb expostulate (to express strong disagreement or protest); adding the noun suffix "-ion" keeps the root spelling "-stul-" intact — expostulate + ion = expostulation, not "expostalation". Contrast this with words where the vowel genuinely changes before a suffix, such as *explain -> explanation*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Nonchalance" — correctly spelt; French borrowing, ends in "-ance".

 

• Option 3: "Circumlocution" — correctly spelt; from "circum-" (around) + "locution" (speech).

 

• Option 4: "Vociferous" — correctly spelt; single "f", ends in "-erous".

 

NOTE

 

• Words retaining their verb-root vowel when forming "-ion" nouns: *expostulate -> expostulation*, *articulate -> articulation*, *stipulate -> stipulation*.

 

• Contrast with words whose vowel changes before a suffix: *explain -> explanation*, *retain -> retention*.

 

• Exam strategy: when a noun is formed from a "-ulate" verb, keep the "u" before adding "-ion" — do not replace it with "a".

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The professor explained how utilitarianisam differs from other ethical theories, encouraging students to weigh the consequences of their decisions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. utilitarianisam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "utilitarianisam". The correct spelling is "utilitarianism", ending in "-anism", not "-anisam". (उपयोगितावाद)

 

• It means the ethical theory that an action is right if it maximizes overall happiness or benefit for the greatest number of people; formed from "utilitarian" + the abstract-noun suffix "-ism".
◦ Example: Utilitarianism judges actions by their consequences rather than by fixed rules.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The professor explained how utilitarianism differs from other ethical theories, encouraging students to weigh the consequences of their decisions.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "ethical" — correctly spelt; from "ethics", single "h".

 

• Option 3: "consequences" — correctly spelt; note the "-quences" ending, not "-quenses".

 

• Option 4: "decisions" — correctly spelt; from "decide", "-sions" not "-tions".

 

NOTE

 

• The suffix "-ism" (forming abstract nouns for doctrines/beliefs) is always spelt "-ism", never "-isam" or "-izm".
◦ *utilitarianism -> utilitarianism*, *capitalism -> capitalism*, *idealism -> idealism*

 

• General rule: long compound abstract nouns ending in "-ism" keep the full spelling of their root adjective/noun before adding the suffix — do not alter internal vowels for "phonetic" spelling.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

The teacher scolded the sluggerd for never completing his homework on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sluggard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "sluggerd", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "sluggard". (आलसी व्यक्ति)

 

• It means a habitually lazy or slow-moving person; related to "slug", the slow-moving mollusc.
◦ Example: Only a sluggard would leave all the packing until the last night.

 

• Spelling key: SLUG + GARD — ends in "-ard" (as in "laggard", "dullard"), not "-erd" or "-art".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "Sluggerd" — incorrect; wrongly uses "-erd" instead of "-ard".

 

• Option 3: "Sluggart" — incorrect; wrongly ends in "-art" instead of "-ard".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" — incorrect; the sentence contains the misspelling "sluggerd", so a replacement is required.

 

NOTE

 

• Related word family: sluggish (adjective, slow-moving), slug (noun, root word) — both keep the base "slug-".

 

• Other "-ard" ending words denoting a type of person: *laggard*, *dullard*, *drunkard*, *coward* — always "-ard", not "-erd" or "-art".
